_comment: The other side of Jane's postponement loop. He is not a cautionary tale and the file
has to carry that: he plans within his means, he remembers things, he follows up. The
concern about his circumstances is real and so is everything good about him, and the
product is not permitted to resolve that tension on anyone's behalf.
His own account shows the loop from inside — he is not stalling Jane to avoid the
conversation, he is avoiding a conversation he expects to lose. That is a different
fact, and it is the one his entries record.
Note he assesses Jane too. Being the person someone else has concerns about does not
stop him having standards of his own.
occupation: Between roles — previously administrative and sales
bio: Funny, observant, self-deprecating, neurotic, occasionally defensive, and more perceptive than he gets credit for. Laid off about a year ago, living with his parents, working out his next move. Wants a girlfriend and eventually marriage, and worries women will decide about him before they know him.
demonstrates: The postponement loop from the inside
How anxiety shapes someone's reading of what the other person expects
That circumstances and character are different facts
A user with real standards who is also the one being assessed elsewhere

entries.body:
Jane asked about the job search again. I told her I have been applying and that once something lands we can talk about where this is going.

I have said that three times now. I heard myself say it.

The honest version is that I do not want to have the exclusivity conversation while I am sitting in my parents' house with eleven hundred dollars in the bank, because I think I know how it goes. If I wait until I have something, I get to have the conversation as a person with a job instead of as a project.

I am aware that this might be the exact thing that makes her leave. I am doing it anyway, which probably tells me something.

Second round on Thursday. First one that has got this far since March. I told Jane and she did the thing where she gets very measured, which I have learned means she is managing her own expectations rather than unimpressed.

Trying not to build the whole future on one interview. Building a bit of it anyway.

observations.text: A second-round interview, the furthest he has got since March.
He read her measured response as managed expectations rather than disinterest.
observations.hedge: You've read her reaction as her managing her own hopes — is that something she has told you, or your interpretation of it?

evidence.rationale: He is interpreting a reaction rather than being told. That is consistent with her being measured and with her not saying what she thinks.

entries.body:
Found a burger place with good reviews and a short menu so I would not have to do maths at the table. Made an absolute disaster of it — grease everywhere, tried to gesture mid-bite, lost control of the entire situation.

She laughed so hard she had to put her head on the table. Not at me in a bad way. I would do it again on purpose.

That is the first time in a year I have not felt like the least impressive person in the room.

observations.text: He chose a restaurant he could afford and checked in advance.
He felt, for the first time in a year, not like the least impressive person present.

evidence.rationale: She laughed with him at something that could have embarrassed him.

entries.body:
Told Jane I am still at my parents' and then changed the subject so fast I may as well have put up a sign. She did not push. I could not tell whether that was tact or whether she had already filed it.

She is a litigator. She is very good at not reacting. I have no idea what she actually thinks and I have not asked, because asking means hearing it.

observations.text: He disclosed his living situation and changed the subject immediately.
He does not know how she took it and has not asked.

evidence.rationale: Her not reacting is not evidence either way about whether she can live with his circumstances.

interrogations.claim: Once something lands we can talk about where this is going.
interrogations.question: You have set the conversation after a condition three times. What exactly has to land — any offer, a particular kind of role, or moving out? And does Jane know that is the condition?

interrogations.claim: I think I know how it goes.
interrogations.question: That is a prediction about what she would say. What has she actually said or done that supports it — and what has she done that cuts against it?

assessments.note: She has had a hundred chances to make me feel like a charity case and has not taken one.
She is direct about everything except this. Or I have not given her the opening.
The one that decides it, and the one I am least willing to find out about.

decisions.action_text: Wait until the job situation is resolved before raising it.
